body.p: The fluid of the renal tubule, lumped from the glomerulus to the urine: the filtered sodium, chloride and water are reabsorbed from it or excreted into the urine. HCTZ increases the excretion of sodium and chloride, by its inhibition of the sodium chloride cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule, a part of the tubule. The id Vloop is historical, the compartment is not the loop of Henle.
The volume the concentration of hydrochlorothiazide in the lumen of the intestine (Cgu_hctz) refers to; it is the volume of the gut Vgu, the model has no volume of the lumen of its own.
This should be the concentration in the kidney, but no kidney compartment in the fluid model.

body.p: The water lost without urine: insensible through the skin and the lungs (about 700 ml a day), the sweat and the feces (about 100 ml each) [Hall2021, Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, chapter 25]. Of the intake of 2.3 l a day the urine is 1.4 l at the reference, the 1.47 to 1.96 l a day of Jeon2012 and Dussol2005; without the loss the urine was the whole intake.

parameter.name: H2O reabsorption from the renal tubule

body.p: Excretion rate water urine.

The urine is at most this fraction of the filtration, the rest of the filtered water is reabsorbed. Without the limit an expanded extracellular fluid (twice its reference) with HCTZ excretes more water than is filtered: the reabsorption of water and sodium turns negative and the integration fails. Within the supported domain the fractional excretion of water stays below 0.09, the limit is not reached.

blockquote.p: 1.0: increased kidney function 1.0: normal kidney function (healthy control) <1.0: decreased kidney function

body.p: Renal function relative to the healthy glomerular filtration rate GFR_base, which is 101 ml/min at 75 kg; a measured clearance of X ml/min is the renal function X/101.

Supported range 0.05 to 2, a GFR of 5 to 202 ml/min. The renal perfusion does not change with the renal function: the GFR is f_renal_function * 0.0763 of the renal blood flow Qki (the model has no hematocrit; with a hematocrit of 0.45 it is f_renal_function * 0.139 of the renal plasma flow, a filtration fraction of 0.28 at 2). Below 0.05 the urine flow approaches 0 and the concentration of HCTZ in the urine is not defined.

GFR per renal blood flow (76.3 ml/l, a ratio of 0.0763). Calibrated so that the healthy GFR is 101 ml/min at the renal blood flow of 1.32354 l/min of 75 kg, the normal GFR of the classes of renal impairment.
Factor scaling cardiac output in cardiac impairment.
Cardiac output per body weight of healthy adults, about 6.5 l/min at 70 kg (Cattermole2017, Patel2021, Collis2001).

The vascular compartments are whole blood: the arterial and the venous blood, the portal and the hepatic vein and the blood of the tissues (V*_plasma). The flows are blood flows, and the species of the vascular compartments (named plasma) are the concentration in plasma with a blood to plasma ratio of 1, which is what the data of plasma are compared with. An erythrocyte uptake of HCTZ (blood to plasma ratio above 1) is not modelled. The value 0.02 is an assumption of the model without a source; the vascular fraction of the kidney and the liver is about ten times larger (ICRP 89, Valentin2002).

parameter.name: hepatic (venous side) fractional tissue blood flow

body.p: Fraction of the cardiac output leaving the liver, the portal (FQgu) and the hepatic arterial flow (Wynne1989, Brown1997, Jones2013, Thompson2009). The hepatic artery is 3.5 % of the cardiac output here, about 6.5 % in ICRP 89 (Valentin2002); without a hepatic clearance of HCTZ the difference does not change the pharmacokinetics.

parameter.name: rest of body fractional tissue blood flow

body.p: Cirrhosis is not supported for HCTZ: it changes only the shunts and the liver tissue, HCTZ has no hepatic clearance (the AUC changes by 0.03 % at 0.9); ascites, the expansion of the extracellular fluid and aldosterone are not in the model.

parameter.name: intrinsic renal clearance of hydrochlorothiazide relative to the GFR

body.p: The intrinsic renal clearance of HCTZ is HCTZEX_f times the GFR (filtration and secretion), acting on the renal venous plasma of a well-stirred kidney: the systemic renal clearance is Qki * CLint/(Qki + CLint), limited by the renal blood flow (2.26 GFR at renal function 1 with HCTZEX_f 2.68, 2.63 at 0.1 and 1.96 at 2). It scales with the body weight as the GFR does (linearly).
The value of KI__HCTZEX_f is the result of the fit PK_20261017_025702__4167a, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.
